clusters.name: Your grandfather Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Walter moving the family across the country in March 1952 and buying an apple orchard, within the year: your grandmother June grew homesick and wrote to her sister daily, then kept to her bed for weeks that first winter; your father Glen fought at school and was sent home twice; your grandfather Walter stopped writing to his brother Harlan after a quarrel over their father's land money and took to the trees from dark to dark while June hardly saw him; he and June rowed over money for new trees. By September 1953, when June joined the church choir and her letters thinned out, the first wave of trouble had settled.

clusters.name: Your grandfather Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard failing in May 1968 when a late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan, within the year: your grandfather Walter drank heavily most nights; he and your father Glen blamed each other for the loan; your father took over the family's money and the talks with the bank; your brother Carl's asthma attacks worsened that winter; you began wetting the bed in April 1969; your grandmother Ida's heart trouble was found and she was told to stop working. By October 1969, when your grandfather stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees, the trouble had lifted.

clusters.name: Your father Glen's job loss at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around your father Glen losing his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975, within the year: he sat out of work most of that year in the truck in the yard for hours; he and your mother Marian had loud fights at night over money; your mother took a second job cleaning offices at night; you stopped eating properly and lost a lot of weight that summer; you kept to your room and said little to your mother; your grandfather Walter drank again after six years off it. By June 1976, when you were eating again and made the track team, the period settled.

clusters.name: Your partner's mother Wilma moving into your house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma moving into your house in January 1990 after selling her farm, within the year: you clashed with her over the children's bedtimes and meals; Sam worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows while Wilma took his side; your son Owen had tantrums at preschool and was sent home twice; Wilma took over Lily's care; you developed eczema on both hands; you and Sam had rows most nights. By August 1991, when Wilma took a flat in town and your eczema cleared over the summer, the period settled.
